data.title: Innovative Industrial Properties Posts Gains, Expands Life Science Reach
data.description:
Innovative Industrial Properties ((IIPR)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Innovative Industrial Properties delivered a broadly positive third-quarter earnings call, led by stronger AFFO, record leasing activity and growing life science investments. Management also highlighted solid liquidity and conservative leverage, although operator financial stress, vacancy, re-leasing delays and uncertainty over cannabis reform remained important risks.

AFFO and Revenue Growth

Third-quarter revenue rose to $64.9 million from $63.3 million in the second quarter. AFFO increased 7% sequentially to $54.8 million, or $1.96 per diluted share, helped by new leases and the recovery of past-due rents, including a $0.15-per-share contribution from Battle Green.

Life Science Investment Expansion

The company closed $275 million of new life science commitments during the quarter. The transactions included an additional $30 million IQHQ preferred equity investment and a $245 million mezzanine loan commitment for Alewife Park, bringing total IQHQ-related commitments to about $545 million.

Alewife Park Loan Economics

The $245 million Alewife Park mezzanine loan is expected to generate an average interest rate of approximately 15.8% over its term. About $111 million was funded at closing, with the remaining $134 million expected to be funded through the fourth quarter of 2027.

Alewife Park Asset Quality and Leasing

Alewife Park is a 27-acre Cambridge, Massachusetts, campus with three buildings totaling 392,000 square feet and two pad-ready sites. The existing buildings are 78% leased to Lila Sciences, while the financing will support tenant improvements, leasing and stabilization.

Greater Portfolio Diversification

Once fully funded, life science investments are projected to represent about 26% of total annualized income. Management said the expansion improves access to lenders and capital sources while reducing the company’s dependence on a cannabis-only portfolio.

Record Quarterly Leasing Activity

The company executed new leases covering approximately 604,000 square feet across six properties during the third quarter. A further 270,000-square-foot lease signed after quarter end lifted total leasing activity since the start of the quarter to about 874,000 square feet.

Year-to-Date Leasing Momentum

Gross leasing activity reached approximately 1.3 million square feet across 12 properties during the first nine months of the year. That represents about 15% of the portfolio, and management said tenant interest remains strong with additional transactions in the pipeline.

Additional Leasing Pipeline

Agreements cover three Colorado properties totaling 72,000 square feet, subject to license transfers and regulatory approvals. Separate agreements for three properties previously leased to 4Front Ventures cover 374,000 square feet, creating a combined potential pipeline of 446,000 square feet beyond executed leases.

Improving Life Science Demand

JLL reported that combined demand in Boston, San Diego, the Bay Area and Raleigh-Durham increased 44% year over year to nearly 8 million square feet in the first quarter of 2026. The improvement was attributed to better biotech funding conditions and the reshoring of biomanufacturing.

Preferred Equity Capital

After the quarter ended, Innovative Industrial Properties completed a public offering of 2.2 million shares of 9.25% Series B preferred stock at $25 per share. The offering generated $54 million in gross proceeds, intended partly to fund the remaining Alewife Park commitment.

Liquidity and Leverage

The company ended the quarter with $142 million of liquidity, excluding the later preferred stock raise. Net debt to adjusted EBITDA was 2.1 times, while net debt represented 19% of total gross assets, supporting management’s description of a conservative capital structure.

Revolving Credit Facility Extension

Following the quarter, the company extended its existing $87.5 million revolving credit facility by 90 days to January 2027. Management said the extension provides more flexibility to evaluate financing alternatives and manage the capital structure.

Expanded Equity Research Coverage

Stifel Nicolaus and Huntington Capital Markets initiated coverage of the company. Their additions brought total equity research coverage to eight firms, potentially increasing visibility among institutional and retail investors.

Cannabis Regulation and Market Developments

The DEA completed its hearing on a proposal to move marijuana from Schedule I to Schedule III. Management said reform could improve industry economics and access to traditional capital, but emphasized that the timing and outcome remain uncertain; Florida also approved 22 additional medical cannabis licenses.

Cannabis Sales Milestones

Massachusetts surpassed $10 billion in cumulative adult-use cannabis sales in September. California has generated nearly $8.4 billion in cannabis tax revenue since 2018, underscoring the scale of the markets served by the company’s tenants.

Portfolio Re-Tenanting Progress

The company regained possession of properties previously leased to Parallel, PharmCann and The Cannabis Company. Management said the transitions create new leasing opportunities, with replacement leases already signed for certain properties, including a Battle Green asset in New York and a 4Front property in Washington.

Capital-Efficient Re-Tenanting

Year-to-date re-tenanting costs were well below $10 per square foot. The figure includes commissions, tenant improvements, landlord work and other related expenses, suggesting that the company has so far managed transitions without heavy capital requirements.

Operator Financial Challenges

Financial pressure remains an issue for some cannabis operators, even as established companies pursue expansion and mergers and acquisitions. The uneven financial health of tenants continues to pose a risk to rent collection and property performance.

Federal Reform Remains Uncertain

The proposed federal rescheduling of marijuana still requires additional administrative review. Management cautioned that neither the timing nor the final outcome is certain, limiting the ability to rely on reform as an immediate improvement to tenant economics.

Vacancy Following Tenant Possessions

Remaining vacancy was slightly more than 800,000 square feet. About two-thirds of that space is tied to two Florida properties previously leased to Parallel, making those assets the largest concentration of the company’s current vacant space.

Re-Leasing May Take Time

Management said the process from identifying a new tenant to lease commencement, license transfer and regulatory approval has historically taken six to 18 months. This timeline could delay the return of vacant properties to income-producing status.

Nonrecurring AFFO Benefits

Management said several third-quarter AFFO benefits will not repeat, including items related to PharmCann, Parallel and Bavarian. The company also does not provide forward guidance on AFFO, making the quarterly result an imperfect measure of ongoing earnings power.

Security Deposits Mostly Exhausted

Of five tenants discussed during the call, four had fully used their security deposits. Some deposits remained for a handful of properties associated with The Cannabis Company, but the limited cushion highlights tenant-level financial pressure.

Leasing Agreements Need Approvals

The additional 446,000 square feet covered by agreements remains subject to due diligence, licensing and regulatory approvals. Management stressed that there is no assurance the discussions and negotiations will ultimately result in completed leases.

Terminated Lease Activity

The company discussed 16 terminated leases, most involving cultivation assets. Nearly half of the related square footage came from two Florida properties recovered from Parallel, with other terminations involving PharmCann, Battle Green and 4Front.

Forward-Looking Guidance

Management does not provide guidance on whether quarterly AFFO will remain above the $1.90 dividend payout. The Alewife Park loan is expected to be funded through the fourth quarter of 2027 at an average rate of about 15.8%, while life science investments are projected to reach roughly 26% of annualized income; an additional $155 million IQHQ opportunity remains possible, subject to capital decisions.

The earnings call showed a company making measurable progress in AFFO, leasing and portfolio diversification. Strong liquidity and life science growth offer support, but vacancy, tenant stress, regulatory uncertainty and the long re-leasing process remain key issues for investors to monitor.

data.title: KREF Earnings Call Highlights Progress and Credit Risks
data.description:
Kkr Reit ((KREF)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

KREF Earnings Call Shows Balance-Sheet Gains Amid Credit Strain

KREF’s earnings call offered a mixed picture. Repayments, liquidity, leverage reduction and progress on legacy assets strengthened the balance sheet, but large quarterly losses, a realized Boston life science loss, refinancing risks and possible higher reserves underscored continuing credit pressure.

Repayments Surpass Full-Year Goal

KREF reported $2.4 billion of repayments year to date, exceeding its $2 billion expectation for the full year. Third-quarter repayments reached $1.2 billion, nearly matching the annual totals recorded in both 2024 and 2025.

Portfolio Rotates Away From Older Loans

More than 80% of year-to-date repayments came from loans originated in 2021 and 2022. Management said this accelerated the portfolio’s natural rotation and reduced exposure to vintages originated during a period of peak valuations.

Progress on Legacy Exposures

KREF said it materially reduced its watchlist, advanced legacy resolutions and addressed its life science portfolio while shifting toward newer loans with stronger credit characteristics. Three additional watchlist loans were resolved during the quarter.

Liquidity Reaches a Historic High

Quarter-end liquidity rose to about $853 million, including $166 million of cash, $53 million of loan repayments held by a servicer and $600 million of undrawn corporate revolver capacity. Management described the position as one of the strongest in KREF’s history and well above its historical average of roughly $600 million.

Leverage Falls Sharply

Strong repayment activity lowered debt-to-equity from 2.6 times to 2.2 times and total leverage from 4.3 times to 3.1 times. Total leverage is now below the company’s historical target range, providing additional balance-sheet flexibility.

CRE CLO Retirement Completed

KREF completed the retirement of its two remaining commercial real estate collateralized loan obligations by exercising optional redemptions. Management said the shrinking collateral pools had made the structures less efficient than other available non-mark-to-market financing options.

New Lending Continues

KREF originated $157 million of loans during the quarter, including a Class A senior housing portfolio secured by four U.S. properties and a Class A Texas office property. Management said credit spreads were relatively stable, financing was readily available and market liquidity remained healthy.

Property Fundamentals Remain Constructive

Management said underlying property fundamentals were generally constructive across most sectors. Tenant demand and a meaningful slowdown in new construction activity continue to support operating conditions, although financing and valuation pressures remain important risks.

KKR Maintains Broad Origination Reach

KKR’s real estate credit team remains active across bank, insurance and debt-fund capital pools. The platform is originating loans across approximately $43 billion of real estate credit assets under management, giving KREF access to a broad lending network.

Lending and Equity Opportunities Expand

Management described lending conditions as attractive because new loans can be made on a reset basis in a higher-rate environment, while supply is declining. KKR remains focused on multifamily and industrial lending, with senior housing also active, and is paying greater attention to value-add and opportunistic multifamily equity investments.

Raleigh Multifamily Asset Improves

KREF said its Raleigh, North Carolina, multifamily asset has been stabilized through stronger cash flow and improved operations. Occupancy and cash flow were described as favorable, suggesting progress at an asset that had previously required closer attention.

Quarterly Losses Weigh on Results

KREF reported a third-quarter 2026 GAAP net loss of $6 million, or $0.11 per share, and a distributable loss of $152 million, or $2.64 per share. Before realized losses and strategic review expenses, distributable earnings were $5 million, or $0.09 per share.

Higher Rates Pressure Borrowers

Management said the recent rise in interest rates has renewed pressure on property values. Borrowers face higher debt-service costs and lower refinancing proceeds, particularly on assets financed at peak valuations in 2021 and early 2022.

Resolutions May Take Longer

KREF expects the current environment to extend resolution timelines and, in some cases, produce additional credit losses. Some transactions once expected to close before year-end are now likely to extend into the first half of 2027.

Reserves Could Rise

Management said difficult liquidity and valuation conditions could lead to higher reserves in the near term as resolutions advance. KREF is marking assets and maintaining current expected credit loss reserves based on market conditions, while acknowledging that some markets remain opaque and illiquid.

Multifamily Refinancing Is a Key Risk

Multifamily loans, particularly from the 2021 and 2022 vintages, are facing pressure from higher rates and lower values. Management said loans at the lower end of the debt-yield range may have the greatest refinancing difficulty, with referenced legacy loans averaging debt yields in the mid-to-high sixes.

Boston Life Science Loan Ends in Loss

KREF assigned its non-recourse Boston life science loan back to the lender after asset values changed. The quarter included a loss on KREF’s portion of the loan, and the asset was removed from the company’s portfolio.

Strategic Review Continues

An independent strategic review committee has retained financial and legal advisers and continues to assess strategic alternatives. Management offered no further details about the process during the call.

Review Expenses Expected to Increase

Strategic review costs primarily consist of financial and legal adviser fees. Management said expenses were back-ended in the third quarter and are expected to increase in the fourth quarter on a full-quarter basis.

Higher Rates Offer Limited Earnings Benefit

KREF said higher rates are not producing a meaningful bottom-line benefit because some asset floors are already near their limits. Floating-rate debt is also broadly matched with floating-rate loans, while real estate-owned assets generate no income and do not benefit from higher rates.

Share Buybacks Effectively Slow

Share buyback activity largely slowed after the strategic review announcement. Management said capital allocation decisions, including repurchases, are among the key matters being considered by the review committee.

Capital Deployment Remains Measured

KREF said it is deploying capital deliberately rather than replacing repayments with new loans on a dollar-for-dollar basis. The company is prioritizing balance-sheet flexibility as it evaluates lending opportunities and works through legacy exposures.

Guidance Points to Caution

Management expects resolution timelines to extend, with some transactions moving into the first half of 2027, and said reserves could increase in the near term. Originations should remain measured, leverage is expected to stay below its historical range in the fourth quarter, and strategic review expenses are set to rise after back-ended third-quarter costs.

KREF enters the next phase with stronger liquidity, lower leverage and a faster exit from older loan vintages. Still, steep quarterly losses, refinancing pressure, potential credit costs and strategic uncertainty leave the company’s recovery dependent on improved property values and successful asset resolutions.

data.title: TRTX Earnings Call Highlights Growth and Credit Resilience
data.description:
Tpg Re Finance Trust ((TRTX)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

TRTX’s earnings call carried a broadly positive tone, supported by strong origination activity, growing net earning assets, higher net interest income, full portfolio performance, improved financing and ample liquidity. Management also acknowledged pressure from elevated rates, weaker acquisition activity, wider multifamily spreads, higher leverage, a $13 million realized loss and a decline in book value per share.

Strong New Investment Activity

TRTX closed $773 million of new investments in the third quarter and increased net earning assets by $600 million. Since September 2025, the company has originated $2.3 billion of loans, equal to nearly 45% of its current portfolio and helping drive 36% year-over-year growth in net earning assets.

Net Interest Income Accelerates

Net interest income rose about 13% from the second quarter, an increase of roughly $3 million, as the loan portfolio expanded. Management said recent originations should make a larger earnings contribution once they are reflected over a full reporting period.

Credit Performance Remains Resilient

Management reported no meaningful volatility in risk ratings or CECL reserves during the quarter. The loan portfolio was 100% performing at period-end, while its weighted average risk rating held steady at 3.0.

Diversified Portfolio Structure

TRTX held 59 loan investments secured by more than 150 underlying properties, representing $5.2 billion of total commitments. The average loan was $88 million, while multifamily and industrial properties accounted for about 75% of the portfolio.

Balance Sheet Optimization Nears Completion

The company said it has largely completed its balance sheet optimization by diversifying funding, extending liability duration, reducing mark-to-market exposure and improving liquidity. About 75% of leverage is funded through series CRE CLOs and a term loan B, providing more stable, long-duration capital.

FL8 CRE CLO Adds Funding Flexibility

TRTX completed its eighth CRE CLO, securitizing about $1 billion of collateral that was approximately 95% multifamily and industrial. The leverage-neutral transaction generated nearly $43 million in net cash proceeds, is expected to reduce funding costs and lifted non-mark-to-market financing to about 85%.

Reinvestment Capacity Supports Growth

The FL8 transaction created a new 30-month reinvestment period. Combined with existing windows in FL6 and FL7, the structure gives TRTX additional flexibility to recycle capital and support earnings growth.

Share Repurchase Authorization Doubled

TRTX exhausted its previous $25 million repurchase plan, buying 1.2 million shares at a weighted average price of $8 for total consideration of $9.3 million. The purchases increased book value per share by $0.04, and the board approved a new $50 million authorization.

Dividend Covered Before Realized Losses

Distributable earnings before realized losses totaled $18.1 million, or $0.24 per diluted common share. That result covered the common dividend for the quarter, although earnings after the realized loss were materially lower.

Lower Funding Costs and Strong Liquidity

The weighted average cost of funds fell to 1.81% from 1.95% a year earlier. Near-term liquidity was $291.6 million, including cash, undrawn secured capacity, revolver availability and CRE CLO proceeds, while unencumbered loans and total available financing capacity provided additional balance sheet flexibility.

Recent-Vintage Loans Improve Positioning

Management said most of the balance sheet was originated during the past two years and was sized for a higher-rate environment. About 80% of multifamily exposure was originated in 2024 or later, and that share could rise toward 90% after expected repayments.

Strong Pipeline, More Controlled Portfolio Growth

The lending pipeline remains strong, with demand continuing in multifamily and industrial markets. As TRTX moves closer to its target leverage and balance sheet size, management expects activity to become more of a one-in, one-out model, potentially making distributable earnings more stable.

REO Portfolio Remains Earnings Positive

Management said the REO portfolio is contributing positively to quarterly distributable earnings rather than weighing on results. TRTX is in the final stages of marketing one multifamily property and has an LOI in place, with no major change to its monetization strategy.

Rate Floors and Spreads Improve Loan Economics

Loan rate floors have been gradually rising from the former general range of 2.5% to 3%. CRE CLO back-leverage spreads were about 25 basis points wider than when FL8 was launched, a shift that is beginning to support wider loan spreads while TRTX’s liabilities remain locked at tighter levels.

Industrial Fundamentals Stay Resilient

Management described industrial fundamentals as resilient, citing positive leasing momentum across the company’s exposure. Industrial spreads remain relatively firm, although transaction activity has been limited because many assets have already been refinanced or otherwise termed out.

Rental Demand Supports Multifamily

The elevated cost of homeownership and higher borrowing costs continue to make renting more attractive than buying for many households. Management said those conditions are supporting strong demand across the multifamily properties in its portfolio.

Covenants Remain in Compliance

TRTX remained in compliance with all financial covenants at the end of the quarter. The result provides reassurance about the company’s financing structure despite increased leverage and challenging real estate conditions.

Inflation and High Rates Remain Headwinds

Management said inflation has been more persistent than expected, extending the period of elevated interest rates and tight financial conditions. Higher borrowing costs, declining property values in some sectors and heavy refinancing needs continue to pressure real estate owners.

Multifamily REO Conversion Produces Loss

Distributable earnings fell to $5.1 million, or $0.07 per diluted common share, after a $13 million realized loss tied to converting a multifamily loan to REO. The property was hurt by weak market conditions, borrower distress and underinvestment in the asset.

Book Value Declines During Quarter

Book value per common share decreased by $0.10 from June 30 to $10.85 at quarter-end. Management attributed the decline mainly to credit loss expense related to portfolio growth and broader macroeconomic conditions.

Leverage Moves Higher

Total leverage increased to 4.03x from 3.32x at June 30. The rise reflected TRTX’s substantial investment activity during the quarter and underscores the importance of disciplined balance sheet management.

Acquisition Activity Continues to Fade

Management said the gap between buyers and sellers, particularly in multifamily, continues to widen and has pushed acquisition activity lower. New acquisitions remain rare, extending a trend that has persisted for the past two or three years.

Deal Closings Take Longer

The period between signing a transaction and closing has lengthened across the market. Management said these extended timelines can put pressure on earnings and add uncertainty to the timing of portfolio growth.

Multifamily Loan Modified After Vacancy Spike

A multifamily property in a Sunbelt market experienced a sharp increase in vacancy linked to migration trends. TRTX modified the loan to give the property a path toward stabilization and provide the borrower with time to execute a recovery plan.

Multifamily Spreads Widen

Management said spreads on newly built Class A-plus multifamily loans were about 15 to 30 basis points wider. Class B and C real estate, particularly multifamily, saw wider spreads of approximately 25 to 50 basis points.

Selective Lending Limits New Acquisitions

TRTX is seeing very little new acquisition activity and said it is passing on 99% of the office, mixed-use and hotel deals it reviews. The approach reflects a focus on asset quality and disciplined underwriting in a difficult market.

Legacy Loans Face Refinancing Pressure

Loans originated in 2021 and earlier are reaching maturity and may require borrowers to contribute cash equity when refinancing. Management cited an institutional Class A transaction where repaying an agency loan would require a new equity infusion.

Forward-Looking Guidance

Management expects recent-vintage multifamily exposure to rise from roughly 80% toward 90% as repayments occur, while higher rate floors and wider market spreads begin to flow into loan economics. The pipeline remains strong, but growth is expected to become more measured through one-in, one-out activity as leverage and balance sheet targets approach; the company also said one multifamily REO is nearing a marketed sale under an existing LOI.

Overall, TRTX delivered strong portfolio growth, improving financing and resilient credit metrics, while maintaining dividend coverage before realized losses. The main risks remain higher leverage, refinancing pressure, weak transaction activity and multifamily credit challenges, but management’s disciplined lending and funding strategy supported a constructive tone on the call.

data.title: Adaptive Biotechnologies Earnings Call Signals Strong Momentum
data.description:
Adaptive Biotechnologies ((ADPT)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Adaptive Biotechnologies delivered a strongly positive earnings call, highlighted by profitability ahead of expectations, accelerating clinical demand and robust pharmaceutical growth. Higher guidance, expanding margins, a larger backlog and favorable multiple myeloma developments outweighed concerns over Medicare pricing pressure, CMS data issues and uncertain milestone timing.

Profitability Arrived Ahead of Expectations

Adaptive reached total-company profitability earlier than expected in the third quarter. Adjusted EBITDA was positive at $14.3 million, while GAAP net income reached $2.8 million, marking a notable improvement in operating performance.

Revenue Growth and Cash Position Strengthened

Total revenue rose 39% year over year to $83.9 million, supported by MRD growth and revenue from the Pfizer rheumatoid arthritis agreement. Adaptive generated $8 million in free cash flow and ended the quarter with approximately $386 million in total cash.

MRD Revenue Beat Expectations

MRD revenue increased 28% to $72.6 million and represented 86% of company revenue. Excluding $6.5 million of milestone revenue recognized a year earlier, core MRD revenue grew 44%, driven by clinical testing and pharmaceutical sequencing.

Clinical Testing Volume Accelerated

Clinical testing volume climbed 46% year over year, helping clinical revenue grow 41%. Adaptive delivered nearly 40,000 clonoSEQ tests in the quarter, a 10% sequential increase, with every reimbursed indication contributing to the expansion.

DLBCL and Multiple Myeloma Led Volume Growth

DLBCL posted the strongest sequential growth, rising 20%, with gains spread across community and academic accounts. Multiple myeloma represented 45% of clinical volume and increased 11% sequentially, reinforcing its importance to the testing business.

Blood-Based Testing Continued to Expand

Blood-based testing rose 68% year over year and 12% sequentially, reaching 51% of total clonoSEQ volume. In multiple myeloma, blood-based tests accounted for 31% of MRD testing, showing broader adoption of less invasive monitoring.

Community Adoption and EMR Integration Improved

Community volume grew 14% sequentially and represented 37% of total volume, up from 31% a year earlier. Nearly half of orders came from EMR-integrated accounts, while 78% of serial monitoring orders due at Flatiron-integrated community accounts had been fulfilled.

Clinician Reach Expanded

About 5,600 clinicians ordered clonoSEQ in the third quarter, a 37% year-over-year increase. That figure represents roughly 40% of U.S. hematology and oncology providers, indicating continued growth in the test’s clinical reach.

Average Selling Price and Coverage Improved

U.S. average selling price was $1,380, up 3% year over year and roughly flat sequentially. Adaptive expanded commercial coverage in DLBCL and MCL, added Medicaid coverage in Illinois and Ohio, and established coverage in states representing about 62% of Medicaid testing volume.

Longer-Term Pricing Opportunity Remained

Management continued to target an average selling price of approximately $1,400 for the full year. Its longer-term goal is $1,700 to $1,800 per test, supported by broader coverage, more frequent testing and a proposed maintenance-testing bundle.

Maintenance Testing Bundle Went to MolDX

Adaptive submitted a technical assessment to MolDX for an additional multiple myeloma maintenance-testing bundle and said discussions were active. The proposal covers five additional tests during maintenance, although the final number of tests and timing remain uncertain.

Updated Guidelines Strengthened clonoSEQ’s Position

Updated NCCN guidelines gave MRD testing greater prominence, specifically named clonoSEQ and preferred an FDA-approved assay with 10^-6 sensitivity. The guidelines also identified testing points during maintenance and surveillance and said MRD results can inform treatment decisions and monitoring.

New Cure Definition Supported Repeated Testing

The International Myeloma Working Group’s new cure definition calls for five years off treatment with sustained MRD negativity, demonstrated by at least four negative assessments. Management said clonoSEQ aligns with the requirements, supporting its role in recurrence monitoring.

Pharma Sequencing Growth Remained Strong

Underlying MRD pharmaceutical sequencing revenue grew 55% year over year when milestones were excluded. Adaptive added 27 new or amended studies, bringing its active global portfolio to 191 studies and underscoring the expanding use of MRD in drug development.

Pharma Backlog Increased Significantly

MRD pharmaceutical backlog reached approximately $270 million, up 34% from $200 million a year earlier. Multiple myeloma represented about 60% of active studies, 65% of backlog and 79% of new bookings during the quarter.

MRD Adoption in Drug Development Expanded

Nineteen multiple myeloma studies now use MRD as a primary endpoint, compared with 12 a year ago. clonoSEQ was used in 23 interventional studies across multiple myeloma, CLL and ALL, while additional testing points and MRD-guided designs increased bookings per study.

Margins and Operating Leverage Improved

Total company gross margin was 76%, while sequencing gross margin increased to 73% from 66% a year earlier. Lab efficiencies after the NovaSeq X transition and higher testing volumes helped lift MRD adjusted EBITDA to $15.1 million from $7 million.

Immune Medicine Separation Progressed

Adaptive said it was working with Morgan Stanley on the separation of its Immune Medicine business. Management remained on track to announce the path forward by year-end, making the separation an important strategic development for investors.

Pfizer Milestone Was Earned

The Immune Medicine business earned a milestone payment from Pfizer after successfully delivering rheumatoid arthritis data under its agreement. Immune Medicine revenue was $11.3 million, primarily from the Pfizer target-discovery deal, while adjusted EBITDA was $3.2 million.

DLBCL Competitive Position Stayed Strong

Management acknowledged competitive noise in DLBCL but expressed confidence in clonoSEQ’s position. It pointed to technology built for blood cancers, established reimbursement, real-world experience involving approximately 9,000 patients and long-standing customer relationships.

GAAP Profitability May Not Persist

Despite third-quarter GAAP net income of $2.8 million, management said it does not currently expect GAAP net income or positive earnings per share in the fourth quarter or for the full year. The comments introduced caution around the durability of the quarter’s profitability.

Medicare Episode Structure Pressured ASP

The Medicare episode rate covers up to four tests over a patient’s lifetime. As physicians monitor patients more frequently, a growing number move beyond that limit, pressuring realized average selling prices, particularly in multiple myeloma.

CMS Preliminary Pricing Data Was Erroneous

Adaptive identified incorrect data submitted to CMS for the clonoSEQ PLA code during the preliminary 2027 rate-setting process. The company said it was working with CMS to correct the information before finalized rates take effect.

Medicaid Remained the Lowest-Paying Segment

Medicaid accounted for about 10% of Adaptive’s payer mix and remained its lowest-paying segment. Even so, Medicaid average selling price increased 26% year over year as coverage expanded across additional states.

Milestone Timing Remained Difficult to Predict

Management said it had no visibility into MRD milestones for the fourth quarter. Milestone timing depends on customers and is difficult to model, although Adaptive reported a healthy pipeline of milestone opportunities over the coming years.

Pharma Revenue Could Remain Lumpy

Adaptive cautioned that pharmaceutical revenue can vary significantly from quarter to quarter because of milestone timing and study activity. The company nevertheless highlighted its growing backlog and expanding study base as important sources of longer-term visibility.

2027 Guidance Was Not Provided

Management did not issue formal guidance for 2027. It said the business is positioned for strong growth in 2027 and beyond, while investors will need to wait for more specific targets and assumptions.

Forward-Looking Guidance

For full-year 2026, Adaptive raised MRD revenue guidance to $276 million-$286 million, including $9 million of milestone revenue, with no further milestones assumed. The midpoint implies 32% MRD growth, or 41% excluding milestones, while clinical volume growth is expected at about 42% and pharma sequencing growth at roughly 25%.

Operating expenses are expected to be approximately $350 million, near the low end of the prior range and about 5% above last year. Adaptive continues to target a full-year average selling price of roughly $1,400 and a longer-term $1,700-$1,800 range, but does not expect GAAP net income or positive EPS in the fourth quarter or full year.

Adaptive Biotechnologies’ quarter showed powerful operating momentum, with profitability, clinical demand, pharma bookings and margins all improving. While reimbursement pressure, pricing uncertainty and uneven milestones remain risks, the raised 2026 outlook and expanding clonoSEQ adoption provided a constructive message for investors.

data.title: Under Armour Earnings Call Signals Recovery Amid Pressure
data.description:
Under Armour Inc – Class C ((UA)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Under Armour’s earnings call presented a mixed picture for investors. Management highlighted better-than-expected adjusted operating income, stronger brand engagement and gains in selected products, but these positives were offset by falling sales, weak footwear demand, elevated inventory, promotions, restructuring costs and lower margin expectations.

Operating Income Beat Outlook

Under Armour met its second-quarter revenue target and exceeded its adjusted operating income forecast. Reported operating income was $15 million, or $25 million excluding restructuring, transformation costs and a litigation reserve reversal, while adjusted diluted earnings per share were approximately breakeven.

Football Cleats Gain Market Share

The company’s American football cleats business grew by double digits during the quarter. Higher average selling prices and market-share gains helped Under Armour become the number two football cleat brand in the United States.

Selected Apparel and Regions Show Strength

Peak Gear and Core Vanish posted double-digit growth, while France and Shawn also continued to expand. HeatGear, outdoor products and sportswear provided additional support, partly offsetting declines across much of the apparel portfolio.

Brand Engagement Improved

Under Armour’s Instagram account generated about 43 million impressions from July through September, up 55% from a year earlier, and 27 million video views, up 126%. TikTok followers surpassed 1 million, while consideration rose more than 90% and brand perception improved over 24% year over year.

Smaller Product Assortment

Under Armour is targeting an almost 50% reduction in SKUs compared with the level when Kevin Plank returned in 2024. Management has also removed more than 60% of materials and increased product commonality, allowing deeper investment in leading products and clearer good, better and best offerings.

Tech Helix Targets Full-Price Sales

Tech Helix is scheduled to launch later this month at $35, using a coil-constructed fabric designed to improve airflow, stretch and drying speed. Management described it as a potential multimillion-unit, full-price program that could eventually become one of the company’s 10 biggest volume drivers.

Armor Short Adds Protection

The Armor Short places targeted padding inside a compression short through patent-pending shield form technology, while preserving mobility. It is expected to launch in December at $80 for adults and $55 for children on UA.com and in 500 DICK’S Sporting Goods stores.

Running Business Builds Credentials

Under Armour’s running business grew in the quarter, alongside selected cleated categories. Athlete Sharon Lokedi placed second in the Chicago Marathon wearing the Velociti Elite 3, cut more than three minutes from her personal best and became the eighth-fastest female marathon runner in history.

Supply Chain and AI Efforts Advance

At a supplier summit, the company focused on shorter lead times, more efficient material use and faster responses to demand. Early artificial-intelligence initiatives are aimed at supply chain, merchandising and marketing, including shortening the path from athlete insight to product launch.

Youth Licensing to Become More Asset-Light

Beginning in fall 2027, Under Armour plans to shift its youth apparel business toward an expanded licensing model with Centric Brands. The move is intended to reduce inventory, working capital and operating complexity while replacing product sales with royalties and preserving earnings and cash contribution.

Global Marketing Becomes More Focused

The company is consolidating global creative direction, content and campaign priorities under the This Is Your Armor platform. Starting with Tech Helix and Armor Short, Under Armour plans to emphasize one major product story each month across social media, digital channels, retail and wholesale.

Revenue Fell Across Regions

Second-quarter revenue declined 7% to $1.2 billion. North America fell 7% on weaker direct-to-consumer traffic and wholesale sell-through, EMEA dropped 9% amid UK traffic issues and distributor timing, and APAC declined 9% because of pressure in China and licensing.

Broad Channel Weakness Persists

Wholesale revenue decreased 6% to $725 million as full-price sell-through weakened and parts of the distributor business struggled. Direct-to-consumer revenue fell 8% to $494 million, including declines of 7% in owned stores and 12% in e-commerce, while licensing revenue dropped 4% to $28 million.

Footwear Remains the Weakest Category

Footwear revenue declined 11% to $234 million, with most categories down despite growth in running and selected cleated products. Apparel fell 6% to $880 million, pressured by fleece and women’s bottoms, while accessories decreased 7% to $105 million.

Gross Margin Slipped

Second-quarter gross margin fell 30 basis points to 47.0%. Foreign exchange reduced margin by 40 basis points, unfavorable channel and regional mix by 35 basis points, and pricing and slightly higher discounting by 20 basis points, outweighing supply-chain and product-mix benefits.

Inventory Exceeds Sales Needs

Inventory ended the quarter at $1.1 billion, up 4% year over year. The roughly $200 million reduction in the revenue outlook left stocks above planned sales needs, prompting lower future buys and targeted sell-through actions that are reflected in the margin outlook.

North America Faces Traffic and Promotional Pressure

Management described softer consumer traffic, a promotional marketplace and broader pressure on sell-through in North America. Other brands clearing inventory have also made the market less healthy than Under Armour would prefer.

UK and China Remain Challenging

Retail traffic continues to be difficult in the United Kingdom, while China remains under pressure, including in licensing. Under Armour said it must improve productivity and product availability across Asia Pacific as market conditions remain dynamic.

Restructuring Costs Continue

Under Armour recorded $13 million under its fiscal 2027 restructuring plan, including $11 million of restructuring charges and $2 million of transformation-related SG&A. Costs incurred so far total $280 million of the projected $300 million to $350 million, with the plan expected to be substantially complete by December 31, 2026.

Liquidity Remains a Priority

The company ended the quarter with $285 million in cash and $190 million drawn under its $1.1 billion revolving credit facility. Management emphasized working-capital discipline, while fiscal 2027 capital spending is expected to be modestly below the prior year.

Fiscal 2027 Revenue Still Expected to Decline

Under Armour maintained its expectation for a mid-single-digit revenue decline in fiscal 2027. North America could fall somewhat more than previously expected, while third-quarter revenue is projected to decline about 8% to 9%, including a low-double-digit drop in North America and a high-single-digit decline in EMEA.

Margin Outlook Was Reduced

The company lowered its fiscal 2027 gross-margin expansion forecast to 170 to 220 basis points from 220 to 720 basis points previously. The revision reflects higher fuel and freight costs, inventory actions, a stronger U.S. dollar and pressures linked to conflict in the Middle East.

External Costs Increased

Under Armour now assumes about $45 million of headwinds related to the ongoing Middle East conflict, compared with its previous $35 million estimate. Management identified logistics and freight as the largest gross-margin pressure, with unfavorable currency translation adding further strain.

Third-Quarter Profitability Near Breakeven

Adjusted third-quarter operating income is expected to range from a $5 million loss to a $5 million profit. Adjusted diluted earnings per share are forecast at a loss of $0.01 to $0.03, reflecting continuing revenue declines and cost pressures before an anticipated stronger fourth quarter.

Fiscal 2027 Guidance Points to Gradual Improvement

For fiscal 2027, Under Armour expects revenue to decline at a mid-single-digit rate and adjusted SG&A to fall at a low-single-digit rate. Gross margin is expected to expand 170 to 220 basis points, including about 150 basis points from IEEPA tariff refunds, while adjusted operating income is forecast at $140 million to $160 million and adjusted diluted EPS at $0.08 to $0.12.

Management expects a better fourth quarter, supported by new products, pricing, channel and product mix, expense discipline and benefits from the youth transition and wholesale initiatives. The outlook also includes about $45 million of Middle East-related headwinds, approximately $44 million of restructuring and transformation costs, and capital expenditures modestly below last year’s level.

Under Armour’s call showed a company making meaningful strategic changes while confronting a difficult operating environment. Product innovation, stronger engagement and tighter costs offer reasons for optimism, but weak demand, excess inventory, margin pressure and restructuring expenses mean investors are likely to focus on execution and evidence of a sustained recovery.

data.title: WEX Earnings Call Highlights Record Growth and Raised Outlook
data.description:
WEX Inc ((WEX)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

WEX delivered a strongly positive third quarter, marked by record revenue, sharp adjusted earnings growth, stronger organic performance and robust cash generation. Mobility pricing improved, Direct AP outperformed, leverage declined and the company raised its outlook, although softer over-the-road volume, travel pressure, delayed implementations and benefits comparisons remained challenges.

Record Revenue and Earnings Growth

WEX reported record third-quarter revenue of $780.1 million, up 12.8% year over year. Adjusted operating income rose 21.6% to $332.5 million, while adjusted EPS increased 33.6% to $6.13.

Underlying Results Beat Expectations

Excluding fuel prices and foreign exchange, revenue grew 4.4%, adjusted operating income increased 6.7% and adjusted EPS climbed 14.3%. Revenue and adjusted EPS also exceeded company guidance, showing the benefit of operating leverage across the business.

Cash Flow Supported Buybacks

Trailing twelve-month adjusted free cash flow reached $764.1 million. WEX repurchased $200 million of shares during the quarter, equal to 85% of quarterly adjusted free cash flow, and bought back another $75 million through October 26.

Leverage and Capital Allocation

WEX reduced leverage to 2.7 times from 2.9 times sequentially, remaining within its 2.5-to-3.0 target range. Management said most adjusted free cash flow will continue to support buybacks while the company weighs acquisitions against the returns available from repurchasing its own shares.

Margins Continued to Expand

Adjusted operating margin expanded by about 310 basis points, helped mainly by higher fuel prices. On a macro-neutral basis, margins improved 90 basis points year over year, keeping WEX on track for more than 100 basis points of second-half expansion.

Credit Quality Remained Healthy

Credit losses improved to 11.7 basis points from 12.1 basis points, in line with prior guidance. Management credited AI, analytics, new data and risk-adjusted credit strategies for supporting stable performance despite significantly higher fuel prices.

Mobility Organic Growth Accelerated

Mobility organic growth rose to 4.4% from 3.1% in the first half, supported by pricing actions and new business wins. Reported mobility revenue increased 20.6%, including the effects of fuel prices and foreign exchange.

Mobility Outlook Improved

Mobility is running ahead of its original 1% to 3% full-year organic growth target. Management now sees organic growth of 3% to 5%, even without assuming a recovery in customer demand.

Pricing Lifted Mobility Margins

Mobility delivered about 260 basis points of organic margin expansion year over year, with additional pricing benefits expected to build. Management said further pricing and margin opportunities remain as the business approaches 2027.

Largest Over-the-Road Customer Renewed

WEX renewed its largest direct over-the-road customer by gallons processed, a global parcel delivery and logistics leader. Management attributed the renewal to WEX’s technology, service quality and understanding of the customer’s operations.

Benefits Posted Moderate Growth

Benefits revenue increased 4.8% to $207.6 million, while SaaS accounts grew 2.8%. HSA accounts rose 7.7%, average HSA custodial cash assets increased 11.2% and custodial investment revenue climbed 7.7%.

HSA Position Remained Strong

WEX remained the nation’s fifth-largest HSA custodian in the 2026 Devenir mid-year report. Its technology powered eight of the report’s top 10 custodians, giving the company further opportunities to increase HSA awareness and adoption.

Corporate Payments Profitability Improved

Corporate payments adjusted operating income grew 7.4%, with a 190-basis-point margin expansion. Segment revenue rose 3.5% to $137.4 million, while total travel volume increased 13.1%.

Direct AP Beat Expectations

Direct AP volume rose 24%, ahead of the previously expected mid-teens growth rate. The product now contributes about 20% of corporate payments revenue, supported by investments in sales capacity and product functionality.

Virtual Card Portfolio Expanded

WEX added new names to its online travel agency portfolio and continued expanding virtual cards beyond travel. Management highlighted the solutions’ broad geographic and industry reach and is exploring agentic commerce through its technology, partners and payment rails.

AI Investment Moved Forward

WEX is deploying AI in fleet intelligence, smaller-fleet account management, software development, claims adjudication and real-time credit decisions. The company has also built an internal solution designed to shorten development cycles and increase team capacity as these efforts scale.

Credit Access Expanded

By combining AI with proprietary credit tools, WEX dynamically increased credit lines for more than 215,000 customers year to date. The effort helped customers manage higher fuel costs while allowing the company to monitor portfolio risk.

Interest and Funding Benefits

WEX Bank uses deposits and Federal Home Loan Bank lines to secure low-cost funding, while its investment portfolio supports higher yields on HSA assets. Management said a 100-basis-point increase in interest rates would benefit revenue by about $30 million, with roughly half coming from Benefits.

Over-the-Road Volume Softened

Over-the-road mobility volume weakened as elevated diesel prices encouraged some customers to shift freight to rail. Higher fuel prices provided a 16-point growth benefit to the segment, while management described the rail shift as a temporary change in customer behavior.

Middle East Conflict Hit Travel

The Middle East conflict created an estimated 1% headwind to corporate payments growth, especially among online travel agency customers in affected regions. Management said the impact would persist while the conflict continues, but the company should lap it next year if conditions remain stable.

Corporate Payments Growth Target Lowered

WEX reduced its full-year corporate payments revenue growth expectation to 4% to 6% from 5% to 7%. The revision reflected the travel impact of the Middle East conflict.

Embedded Payments Faced Delays

Delayed embedded-payments implementations partly offset the strong Direct AP performance. Management said products are selling well and the pipeline remains strong, but customers are taking longer to build the required connections to WEX systems.

Prior-Year Items Weighed on Payments

Corporate payments continued to face comparisons with the prior year’s scheme-incentive renegotiation and one-time revenue items. Management cited an additional 140-to-150-basis-point scheme drag and an approximately two-point impact from the one-time item in the fourth quarter.

Benefits Account Comparisons Stayed Difficult

Benefits SaaS account growth of 2.8% reflected a tough comparison from a large UAW trust portfolio added in the prior year, along with previously disclosed account closures. Both pressures were expected to continue through the fourth quarter, although the closures had little effect on revenue or income.

Lower Rates Pressured Benefits

Benefits faced an approximately 130-basis-point year-over-year drag from lower interest rates in the quarter, alongside a broader rate headwind of more than one percentage point. Moving about $300 million of assets from third-party banks to WEX Bank also shifted revenue between reporting lines.

Fuel-Related Charge-Offs May Rise

Management said higher fuel-cost charge-offs would begin reaching the income statement in the fourth quarter because losses typically follow card activity by about two quarters. Credit performance remains within the range set at the start of the year, and the overall portfolio was described as strong.

Travel Mix Reduced Interchange

Corporate payments’ net interchange rate declined by one basis point as seasonal travel increased. Travel transactions generally carry lower interchange rates than non-travel transactions, but management expects yields to move back toward earlier-year levels as travel cools.

Margin Investment Remains Balanced

Management said it remains pleased with the margin trajectory and expects more than 100 basis points of expansion in the second half. However, it does not expect margin expansion to accelerate next year as WEX balances investment in future growth with profitability.

Raised Fourth-Quarter and Full-Year Guidance

WEX expects fourth-quarter revenue of $760 million to $780 million and adjusted EPS of $5.67 to $5.87. Full-year revenue guidance is $2.97 billion to $2.99 billion, with adjusted EPS of $21.28 to $21.48, representing increases of $96 million in revenue and $1.50 in EPS versus the midpoints of the prior ranges.

At the midpoint of fourth-quarter guidance, WEX expects 5% organic revenue growth, with no mobility demand recovery assumed. Mobility organic growth is projected at 3% to 5%, corporate payments revenue growth at 4% to 6%, and second-half macro-adjusted margin expansion above 100 basis points; the outlook includes current rate assumptions, a 1% Middle East conflict headwind and no buybacks beyond the third quarter.

WEX Leaves Call With Strong Momentum

WEX’s quarter combined record financial results, accelerating mobility performance, Direct AP momentum and disciplined capital allocation. While fuel-driven behavior, travel disruption, implementation delays and benefits comparisons create near-term risks, the raised outlook and improving underlying growth point to a constructive earnings trajectory.

data.title: WhiteHorse Finance Earnings Call Shows Gains and Risks
data.description:
WhiteHorse Finance ((WHF)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

WhiteHorse Finance’s earnings call delivered a broadly constructive message, led by a second straight quarterly NAV gain, stronger credit metrics and a portfolio heavily weighted toward senior-secured loans. However, GAAP net investment income remained below the distribution, several investments stayed on nonaccrual, and refinancing needs, soft M&A activity and a paused buyback program added caution.

NAV Rose for a Second Quarter

NAV per share increased to $11.82 at the end of the third quarter from $11.77 in the second quarter, a gain of about 0.4%. Approximately $0.09 per share of realized and unrealized gains more than offset a roughly $0.04 per-share shortfall between net investment income and distributions.

Chase Products and Playmonster Lifted Portfolio Gains

Net realized and unrealized gains totaled about $2.1 million, or $0.096 per share. Chase Products contributed a $1.3 million markup and Playmonster added $0.7 million, while other markups were partly offset by a $0.7 million markdown on Arcserve.

Core Investment Income Improved

Core net investment income rose to $4.8 million, or $0.224 per share, from $4.7 million, or $0.217 per share, in the prior quarter. The increase pointed to modestly stronger underlying earnings, even as reported GAAP results were affected by unusual expenses.

Credit Quality Strengthened

Nonaccrual investments fell to 2% of the debt portfolio at fair value from 3.6%, and to 4.4% at cost from 6.9%. Outward Hound returned to accrual status after its restructuring, and management reported no new additions to nonaccrual.

Buybacks Added to NAV

Since launching its repurchase program in the fourth quarter of 2025, WhiteHorse has bought about 1.8 million shares at an average price of approximately $7.36. Management estimates those purchases increased NAV by roughly $0.33 per share.

Incentive Fee Waiver Extended

The adviser extended its voluntary incentive fee waiver through the fourth quarter of 2026, lowering the applicable rate from 20% to 17.5%. Cumulative waivers have represented about $530,000, or $0.024 per share, in fees not charged to the company.

Chase Products Remained Ahead of Plan

Chase Products continued to perform better than expected, and WhiteHorse is actively pursuing a sale after receiving constructive interest from potential buyers. Management said it currently expects the process to conclude within two to four months, although timing and completion are not assured.

Playmonster Demand Rebounded

Playmonster saw a material recovery in demand across several product lines, supporting stronger results and a $0.7 million valuation increase. Management indicated that a sale process could be pursued during the first half of 2027.

Deployment Stayed Disciplined

Third-quarter gross capital deployments were $21 million, including two new originations totaling $14.8 million and $6.2 million of add-on funding. Repayments and sales of about $10 million produced net deployments of approximately $10.9 million before transfers to the STRS JV, with new loans averaging 3.6 times EBITDA and all being first lien.

STRS JV Continued to Support Growth

WhiteHorse transferred five investments totaling $21.4 million to the STRS JV in exchange for a $7.2 million net JV investment and about $14.2 million in cash. The venture generated approximately $3.5 million of income for WhiteHorse, up from $3.2 million in the prior quarter, and delivered a low-teens return on equity.

Portfolio Mix Remained Conservative

First-lien, senior-secured investments represented 98.8% of the debt portfolio at quarter end. Nonsponsor investments accounted for about 42% of fair value, while the weighted average effective yield on income-producing debt rose to 11% from 10.8%.

Credit Markets Were Constructive

Management described 2026 credit markets as favorable, with most deals carrying loan-to-value ratios below 55% and solid cash-flow coverage. Pricing on many 2026-vintage transactions was 50 to 75 basis points higher than in 2025 and 2024, while nonsponsor loans generally offered 3 to 4.5 times leverage and pricing of SOFR plus 600 basis points or more.

Selective Software Deals Offered Better Terms

Lender over-allocation to software is creating opportunities with lower enterprise values, lower loan-to-value ratios and much less leverage. WhiteHorse said these investments can offer pricing 100 to 150 basis points above comparable nonsoftware deals, citing a fourth-quarter transaction at 3.8 times leverage and 625 basis points over SOFR.

Platform Volume and Capacity Increased

Investment volume across the WhiteHorse platform was estimated to be at least 50% higher than 2025 levels. After quarter end, the BDC closed a sponsor investment of about $65 million, while the STRS JV completed a $4.9 million investment; pro forma capacity stood at approximately $22 million for the JV and $25 million on the BDC balance sheet.

Distributions Included a Special Payment

The board declared a fourth-quarter base distribution of $0.25 per share and a $0.17 special distribution tied to undistributed taxable income from 2025. Including the special payment and distributions already made during the year, current spillback income was estimated at approximately $14.3 million.

Balance Sheet Stayed Above Regulatory Levels

The asset coverage ratio for borrowed amounts was 177.3% at September 30, comfortably above the 150% regulatory minimum. Gross leverage eased to 1.29 times from 1.30 times, while net effective debt-to-equity was 1.20 times compared with 1.19 times in the prior quarter.

GAAP Income Fell Below the Distribution

Third-quarter GAAP net investment income declined to $4.4 million, or $0.207 per share, from $4.7 million, or $0.217 per share. The result was below the $0.25 base distribution, with the gap reflecting about $450,000 of nonrecurring noncash expenses and write-offs.

Quarterly Expenses Increased

Total expenses rose to $10.4 million from $9.7 million in the previous quarter. The increase was driven mainly by nonrecurring shelf-registration and ATM-program costs, along with approximately $0.1 million in independent director fees related to the special committee.

Three Issuers Remained on Nonaccrual

Although overall nonaccrual measures improved, Camarillo Fitness, New Cycle Solutions and Playmonster remained on nonaccrual at quarter end. Their continued status shows that credit recovery remains uneven across the portfolio.

Outward Hound Faced Operating Pressure

WhiteHorse completed an Outward Hound restructuring in early July, converted part of the debt into equity and took majority ownership and board control. Management said the pet products market remains difficult and that it is working with the company on revenue growth and cost reduction.

Arcserve Experienced Weakness

The $0.7 million Arcserve markdown reflected several quarters of relative business weakness. The company remains cash-flow positive, and WhiteHorse is working with management on measures intended to accelerate growth.

Camarillo Fitness Sale Process Began

The valuation mark for Camarillo Fitness reflected expected proceeds from selling its underlying locations. The process is active, with capital expected to return as individual locations are sold and cash is collected.

Portfolio Ratings Moderated

About 84.8% of portfolio positions carried a risk rating of 1 or 2, down from 86.6% in the prior quarter. The change suggests that, despite improving nonaccrual statistics, some investments are experiencing increased operating or credit pressure.

December Debt Maturities Remained a Focus

WhiteHorse has $85 million of unsecured notes due in December 2026, including $10 million of 5.375% notes due December 4 and $75 million of 4% notes due December 15. Management said it is discussing financing options and feels confident it can address the maturities, but provided no further details.

Refinancing May Cost More

Management noted that the maturing notes were issued in 2021 or earlier, when borrowing costs were lower. Comparable fixed-rate BDC financing was described as generally above 7%, likely around 7.5% to between 7% and 8%, creating a potential cost increase.

Share Repurchases Were Paused

The company is not currently repurchasing shares while its special committee evaluates strategic alternatives. Management said buybacks could be reconsidered if the review does not lead to a successful transaction.

Strategic Review Remained Unresolved

The special committee continues to examine alternatives that could include a sale or another corporate transaction. No timetable has been established, and management emphasized that there is no assurance the review will result in a transaction being pursued or completed.

M&A and Some Deal Volumes Were Soft

Management said third-quarter M&A activity was flat to lower than the prior year and expected fourth-quarter activity to decline. Nonsponsor deal flow was also lighter, while some opportunities did not meet the BDC’s pricing threshold or fit the STRS JV’s acquisition criteria.

Some Credits Needed Equity Support

A small number of portfolio companies experienced operating weakness, with only a couple facing covenant defaults and requiring equity injections. Sponsors or other stakeholders had agreed to provide additional equity support for those investments.

WhiteHorse Avoided Riskier Software Deals

The company generally avoided software transactions involving broken capital structures or significant artificial-intelligence risk. Instead, it is focusing on new-money buyouts backed by fresh equity, lower leverage, covenant protection and limited or no AI exposure.

Forward-Looking Guidance

Management expects the Chase Products sale process to potentially finish within two to four months and said a Playmonster sale could be pursued in the first half of 2027. The fourth-quarter base distribution is $0.25 per share, payable January 6, 2027, while the $0.17 special distribution is payable December 10, 2026; management also expects to keep evaluating distributions against core earnings.

WhiteHorse Finance enters the next phase with improving NAV, stronger aggregate credit metrics and meaningful investment capacity. Still, below-distribution GAAP income, troubled holdings, higher potential refinancing costs and an unresolved strategic review leave investors with clear positives alongside important risks.

Veracyte reported third-quarter revenue of $152 million, up 15% from a year earlier, while testing volume also rose 15% to about 52,700 tests. GAAP net income reached $31.5 million, and adjusted EBITDA was $41.2 million, or 27.2% of revenue, above the company’s 25% long-term target.

Strong Cash Generation

The company generated $40.3 million in operating cash flow during the quarter. Veracyte ended the period with $371 million in cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments, even after paying $150 million for the Convergent Genomics acquisition.

Testing Revenue and Margins

Testing revenue increased 15% to $146 million, while testing volume rose 13% to 49,500 tests. Average selling price grew 1% to $2,960, or about 2% on a normalized basis, and non-GAAP gross margin expanded 90 basis points to 73.7%.

Afirma Outperformance

Afirma delivered about 19,000 tests in the quarter, up 12% year over year, supported by deeper use among existing physicians and continued market-share gains. The V2 transcriptome workflow lowered the no-result rate and contributed about 300 basis points to annual volume growth.

Afirma Guidance Raised

Veracyte raised its full-year 2026 Afirma revenue growth forecast to 16%, from a previous range of 12% to 14%. The change reflects strong third-quarter performance, prior-period collections, improving pricing and an expected 3% benefit from a lower no-result rate.

Decipher Growth and Clinical Evidence

Decipher prostate testing reached nearly 30,000 tests in the third quarter, representing 12% annual growth. Veracyte highlighted new predictive evidence from the NRG RTOG 0815, STAMPEDE and ENZAMET studies across intermediate-risk, very-high-risk nonmetastatic and metastatic prostate cancer.

Decipher Pipeline Expands

The GUIDANCE and PREDICT-RT Phase 3 trials are fully enrolled, while preliminary findings from the NCI-sponsored Phase 3 and G-MAJOR low-risk studies could arrive as early as next year. Veracyte is also adding PORTOS, PTEN and PAM50 signatures to its molecular features report and expects an initial DPAI publication in the next few quarters.

Urology Investment Increases

Veracyte plans to expand its urology organization by 30% next year, adding field representatives, medical science liaisons and sales leaders. The investment is intended to support Decipher prostate while increasing coverage for Decipher Bladder, TrueMRD and eventually UroAmp.

Prosigna Launch and Differentiation

The company launched Prosigna in the United States after the OPTIMA Phase 3 results delivered Level I evidence. The study identified more than two-thirds of clinically high-risk women who could safely avoid chemotherapy, adding to support from 157 Prosigna publications and more than 1,200 publications on its PAM50 classifier.

Prosigna Demand and Reimbursement

Early U.S. demand for Prosigna was encouraging, and the dedicated medical oncology team is expected to reach 15 representatives by year-end. Medicare reimbursement is now available for eligible postmenopausal women with early-stage ER-positive breast cancer and zero to three positive nodes, while international product revenue rose 40%.

Bladder Cancer Portfolio

The Convergent Genomics acquisition added UroAmp, a urine-based tumor DNA platform, to Veracyte’s bladder cancer portfolio. Together with tissue-based Decipher Bladder and blood-based TrueMRD, the company aims to cover diagnosis, treatment response, recurrence monitoring and post-treatment surveillance.

UroAmp Evidence and Commercial Plan

UroAmp has nine peer-reviewed publications and more than 40 abstracts and posters, with four additional abstracts accepted for a urology meeting. Data from the prospective INSIGHT trial have also been accepted for publication, supporting the company’s plan to introduce its first UroAmp application in late 2028.

TrueMRD Reaches the Market

Veracyte launched its first commercial TrueMRD test earlier this year after securing Medicare reimbursement for recurrence monitoring in muscle-invasive bladder cancer following radical cystectomy. The test uses whole-genome sequencing for both initial landmark testing and ongoing monitoring.

One-Millionth Patient Milestone

Veracyte served its one-millionth patient during the quarter. Management described the milestone as evidence of the company’s growing reach and the practical impact of its diagnostic tests.

Share Repurchase Authorized

Veracyte’s board authorized a share repurchase program of up to $100 million. The authorization gives management another way to return capital to shareholders while signaling confidence in the company’s financial position.

Long-Term Portfolio Opportunity

Management expects growth to accelerate through 2027, 2028 and beyond as Decipher evidence expands across risk groups and newer breast and bladder products gain traction. The company continues to view 80% market share and 80% penetration as achievable long-term goals for Decipher.

Decipher Volume Misses Expectations

Decipher prostate volume was about 1,000 tests below expectations in the third quarter. Even so, the business completed nearly 30,000 tests and maintained 12% year-over-year growth.

Decipher Volume Outlook Reset

Veracyte reset its expected annual incremental Decipher volume growth to 12,000 to 15,000 tests. Management described the lower end of that range as a reasonable near-term floor, compared with its previous expectation of about 20,000 incremental tests.

Growth Normalization in Low-Risk Patients

Management said earlier NCCN guideline changes created a temporary acceleration and two years of unusually strong Decipher growth. The latest low-risk guideline shift, along with more patients choosing surveillance without additional testing, has slowed growth in that segment to the single digits.

Competition Pressures Sales Efforts

Digital pathology and artificial intelligence tools have attracted physician attention and forced the sales organization to spend more time explaining the evidence behind molecular testing. Veracyte said this activity has distracted the commercial team and reduced time available for core selling efforts.

2026 Revenue Guidance Lowered

The company narrowed and reduced its 2026 revenue outlook to $590 million to $593 million, representing 14% to 15% growth. Testing revenue is now expected to reach $571 million to $573 million, or 16% growth, below the previous forecast of $576 million to $582 million.

Moderated 2027 Revenue Outlook

For 2027, Veracyte expects total testing volume to grow about 10%, but revenue growth to be only in the mid-single digits. The difference reflects roughly 200 basis points from prior-period collection comparisons and another 200 basis points from product mix, including lower-ASP Prosigna and bladder testing.

2027 Profitability Below Long-Term Goal

Management expects full-year 2027 adjusted EBITDA margin of about 22%, below its unchanged 25% long-term objective. The first quarter is expected to be weaker because of expense timing, with margins improving toward 25% by the end of the year.

Prosigna Coverage Constraints

Current Medicare coverage for Prosigna is limited to postmenopausal patients with zero to three positive nodes. Coverage for patients with four to nine positive nodes could take years to expand, while broader premenopausal coverage will require commercial contracts, keeping current average pricing near cost.

New Products Have Limited Near-Term Impact

Prosigna and TrueMRD are expected to make modest revenue contributions in 2027 because new tests typically require time to gain adoption. Management said bladder products should become more meaningful contributors in 2028 and beyond.

UroAmp Faces Timing and Reimbursement Hurdles

UroAmp commercialization is not expected until late 2028, and reimbursement remains challenging when multiple tests are performed for the same patient. Veracyte is developing additional evidence to support payment for repeated testing.

International Priorities Shift

Veracyte remains committed to making Decipher available internationally, but its priorities have shifted somewhat toward bladder cancer after acquiring Convergent Genomics. The company said this reflects the potential of the expanded portfolio alongside continued growth in its core business.

Forward-Looking Guidance

For 2026, Veracyte expects revenue of $590 million to $593 million, testing revenue of $571 million to $573 million, Afirma growth of 16% and adjusted EBITDA above 26%. For 2027, management anticipates 10% volume growth, mid-single-digit revenue growth and a 22% adjusted EBITDA margin, with Decipher adding 12,000 to 15,000 tests annually.

Veracyte’s call combined strong current results with a more cautious near-term outlook. Afirma, clinical evidence and the bladder portfolio remain important growth drivers, but slower Decipher expansion, competitive pressure and reimbursement limits point to a measured path for revenue and margins.
