data.title: Q2 Holdings Earnings Call Signals Growth and Margin Momentum
data.description:
Q2 Holdings ((QTWO)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Q2 Holdings delivered a strongly positive quarter, beating its revenue and adjusted EBITDA targets while posting record margins and stronger cash generation. Management highlighted robust bookings, renewals, credit union wins, fraud demand, relationship pricing and early AI adoption, although it acknowledged pressure in discretionary services, higher near-term investment and uncertainty around AI economics at scale.

Leadership Continuity With Price Named Co-CEO

Q2 Holdings appointed CFO Jonathan A. Price as co-CEO alongside Matthew Flake, while he continues leading the finance function. Price will join the board as the company searches for a new CFO, with management describing the arrangement as supportive of long-term continuity and normal day-to-day operations.

Revenue and Profit Beat Expectations

Third-quarter revenue reached $225.8 million, up 12% from a year earlier and 3% sequentially, while adjusted EBITDA was $67.8 million. Free cash flow totaled $55 million, and both revenue and adjusted EBITDA finished above the high end of company guidance.

Recurring Revenue Remains the Growth Engine

Subscription revenue increased 14% year over year and 3% sequentially, accounting for 83% of total revenue. Total annual recurring revenue rose 11% to $989 million, while subscription ARR grew 13.5% to $846 million, supported by new customer launches and expansion among existing clients.

Backlog and Bookings Build Momentum

Ending backlog rose 10% year over year to $2.8 billion, compared with $2.5 billion a year earlier, and increased $5 million sequentially. Growth reflected new, expansion and renewal bookings, including seven Tier 1 and enterprise wins and meaningful activity among Tier 2 customers.

Credit Unions Produce Major Digital Wins

Credit unions were an important source of digital banking momentum during the quarter. An institution with roughly $3 billion in assets selected Q2’s platform in the quarter’s largest deal by contracted recurring revenue, while a credit union of about $10 billion chose its commercial digital banking product.

Risk, Fraud and Pricing Products Expand

A bank with more than $60 billion in assets expanded its relationship with Q2 through several risk and fraud products, including SentriX, an AI-based account takeover solution and user activity monitoring. Bookings also benefited from digital banking and relationship pricing, broadening the company’s revenue opportunities.

Margins Reach Record Levels

Non-GAAP gross margin climbed to 62.6%, up from 57.9% a year earlier and about 30 basis points sequentially. Adjusted EBITDA rose 39% year over year to $67.8 million, lifting the margin to 30%, an expansion of about 580 basis points from the prior-year period.

Cash Generation Strengthens a Debt-Free Balance Sheet

Operating cash flow increased to $65 million from $46 million, while free cash flow rose 48% year over year to $55 million, equal to about 81% of adjusted EBITDA. Cash, equivalents and investments reached $123 million, and Q2 remained debt free after retiring its convertible notes in June.

Buybacks Preserve Capital Allocation Flexibility

Q2 repurchased approximately $39 million of its stock during the quarter and had about $336 million remaining under its authorization. Management said it intends to balance organic investment and possible acquisitions with disciplined share repurchases, preserving flexibility as opportunities develop.

Full-Year 2026 Outlook Raised

The company lifted its full-year 2026 revenue forecast to $888 million-$892 million, implying approximately 12% growth. Adjusted EBITDA guidance increased to $253 million-$256 million, representing about 28.6% of revenue at the midpoint and roughly 500 basis points of annual margin expansion.

2027 Framework Remains Constructive

Q2 reiterated its 2027 framework for subscription revenue growth of 12.5% to 13% and adjusted EBITDA margin expansion of 150 to 200 basis points. Management expects to finish 2026 at approximately a Rule of 43, above the Rule of 40, and expects 2027 to meet or exceed that level.

AI Products Gain Early-Adopter Interest

At its Dev Days event, Q2 previewed broader capabilities for Q2 Code and Q2 Assistant, including development support and multistep service workflows. Early-adopter programs continued to attract customers, with User Activity Monitoring reaching nearly 20 financial institutions, about twice the company’s expectation.

AI Pricing Shows Early Promise

Management said early economics for its AI solutions appeared positive under a hybrid model combining subscription fees with variable, value-based charges. Token caps and other safeguards are designed to protect margins from unexpectedly heavy usage, while pricing has not yet emerged as a major obstacle.

Fraud Intelligence Becomes a Major Investment

Q2 is investing heavily in a fraud intelligence platform that combines its data, transaction signals, digital-session visibility and products such as User Activity Monitoring. Management sees fraud as a significant customer problem and believes its digital banking relationships provide a strong foundation for addressing it.

Relationship Pricing Demand Remains Strong

The complexity of the current interest-rate environment is driving demand for relationship pricing tools. Q2 said it sits on data tied to approximately $2 trillion of loans and $2 trillion of deposits, while nine of North America’s 15 largest banks use its relationship pricing product.

Renewal Economics Improve Across Key Measures

Third-quarter renewals were described as the strongest of the year across price increases, cross-selling, annual or inflation-linked increases and contract duration. These trends also exceeded the strong renewal quarters of the second half of 2025, as customers increasingly discuss digital banking, fraud and AI transformation.

Innovation Studio Expands Its Partner Network

Innovation Studio had a strong first nine months across bookings, revenue and adoption, with more than 200 partner products. Q2 said AI is increasingly being built into both new and existing offerings, creating a positive halo as the company distributes partner technology and participates in the resulting economics.

Pipeline Spans Banks, Credit Unions and Products

Management said its pipeline remains strong across retail and commercial digital banking, banks and credit unions, fraud and relationship pricing. Further growth is expected from existing-customer expansion as well as institutions growing organically or through mergers and acquisitions.

Discretionary Services Face Pressure

Total nonsubscription revenue rose about 3% year over year, largely because of professional-services timing. Q2 nevertheless continued to expect pressure in more discretionary services, with nonsubscription revenue projected to decline slightly in the fourth quarter and remain roughly flat for the full year.

Investment Spending Will Weigh on Fourth-Quarter Margins

Some planned investments began late in the third quarter and will be fully reflected in the fourth quarter. As a result, third-quarter adjusted EBITDA margins benefited from some outperformance versus the coming period, while Q2 continues spending on sales, Innovation Studio, fraud, AI and other product priorities.

AI Economics Still Need to Prove Their Scale

Although early-adopter gross-margin results were encouraging, Q2 has not yet tested the economics at broad scale. Management said infrastructure and computing costs remain uncertain as products move toward general availability, leaving pricing and profitability to be validated with wider usage.

AI Revenue Is Not Yet in the Forecast

The potential revenue contribution from User Activity Monitoring and other AI products remains too early to quantify because the offerings are not generally available and early-adopter pricing is experimental. Q2 has therefore excluded potential AI upside from its current 2027 outlook.

Helix Fintech Growth Remains Limited

Helix’s marquee and high-volume customers remain healthy, renewing and expanding, but they are not investing at the pace seen three or four years ago. The fintech and nontraditional market has been slow since 2023, and Q2 has yet to see enough traction with traditional institutions to report meaningful progress.

Renewals Face Seasonal Third-Quarter Comparisons

Management noted that the third quarter is typically lighter for renewals and faced a tougher comparison because the prior-year period was not light. A seasonal increase in fourth-quarter activity is expected, but executives emphasized that execution and renewal economics matter more than any single quarter’s backlog.

Fraud Market Potential Remains Hard to Measure

Q2 said its previously cited $4 billion fraud and risk total addressable market may prove conservative as monitoring needs and use cases expand. However, management said it cannot yet quantify the additional monetization opportunity or its impact on the overall market size.

Fourth-Quarter and 2026 Guidance

Q2 forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $226 million-$230 million and adjusted EBITDA of $62.4 million-$65.4 million. For 2026, it expects subscription revenue growth of about 14.5%, nonsubscription revenue to be roughly flat for the year, free-cash-flow conversion of at least 90% and revenue and adjusted EBITDA within its raised ranges.

The earnings call showed Q2 Holdings combining dependable recurring-revenue growth with sharper profitability and cash generation. Strong bookings, renewals, product expansion and early AI interest support the investment case, while services pressure, heavier spending, uncertain scaled AI economics and slow Helix traction remain the main risks for investors to monitor.

Management also highlighted robust cash generation, rising automation and AI adoption, encouraging client returns, and stronger full-year guidance, while noting that fourth-quarter comparisons and calendar effects could create volatility.

Revenue Growth Remains Solid

GAAP net income reached $133 million, or $2.99 per diluted share, while non-GAAP net income climbed 37% to $150 million, or $3.37 per share. Adjusted EBITDA was $268 million, equal to 49.3% of revenue, as higher gross margins and lower operating costs lifted profitability.

Free Cash Flow Provides Financial Strength

Paycom generated $536 million of free cash flow during the first nine months of 2026, reinforcing the company’s ability to convert earnings into cash. Management described the cash generation as sustainable and durable, providing flexibility for investment, debt repayment, dividends, and share buybacks.

Automation and AI Adoption Accelerate

Clients are adopting more automation as Paycom expands its automated decisioning logic and AI capabilities. Management said earlier investments in data centers, AI technology, and GPUs are benefiting both clients and Paycom, while customers do not pay separately for system tokens.

IWant Shows Measurable Client Value

Paycom’s IWant assistant is enabled across its client base and has handled millions of queries, with usage about 65% above the end of 2025. Forrester found that mid-market users could achieve more than 400% ROI and save thousands of employee, manager, and executive hours without incremental costs.

Decisioning Logic Delivers Direct Savings

Paycom cited a business that eliminated $360,000 in unmanaged paid time off after using Don. The customer operated across 73 locations in 12 states, where manual approvals and negative time-off balances had previously created substantial waste.

Asset Management Gains Traction

The company’s asset management product, launched in the prior quarter, had attracted approximately 300 or more clients. Built-in decision logic helps customers track, recover, and redeploy assets they already own, supporting better control of existing resources.

Product Pipeline Builds Momentum

Paycom released more solutions in the past year than in any previous 12-month period, with several additional products being tested or used by selected clients. Management characterized 2027 as potentially transformative as new products and AI capabilities move toward broader release.

Data Centers Offer Strategic Control

Paycom operates one of only a handful of Tier 4 data centers in the United States, giving it greater control over technology, security, and costs. Management said its infrastructure supports client returns and operational efficiency across research, development, and service operations.

Service Efficiency Improves Satisfaction

Strong product usage and continued customer-service investment are lifting satisfaction and net promoter scores. Automation is also allowing service employees to spend less time on inbound support and more time on proactive analysis and outreach designed to improve client returns.

Sales Execution Supports Market Opportunity

Management said its newest sales representatives are performing better than any prior group and that overall sales activity is meeting the company’s goals for the year. Prospects are also showing greater willingness to automate additional decisions, keeping sales and marketing central to the growth strategy.

Share Repurchases Reduce the Share Count

Shares outstanding ended the quarter at about 44 million, nearly 20% below the approximately 55 million reported at the end of the third quarter of 2025. Paycom repurchased about 11.5 million shares over that period and retained $1.65 billion under its buyback authorization after purchasing $3 million of stock during the quarter.

Debt Falls as Dividends Continue

Paycom repaid $150 million on its revolving credit facility during the quarter and ended with $194 million in cash and cash equivalents alongside $750 million outstanding under the facility. It also paid roughly $17 million in dividends, while the board approved a subsequent quarterly dividend of $0.375 per share.

Client Funds Held Continue to Grow

The average daily balance of funds held for clients was approximately $2.7 billion in the third quarter, up 7% from the prior-year period. These balances remain an important source of financial support as Paycom expands its customer base and payroll platform.

Infrastructure Improves R&D Economics

Management said research and development spending declined even as Paycom continued to enhance its products, helped by sharper focus and newer technologies. Infrastructure investments made previously have also produced about $100 million in R&D savings and $30 million in avoided third-party fees.

Project ARC Boosts Performance

Project ARC created a foundation for broader automation in areas such as punch changes, time-card approvals, and expense decisions. Paycom said one enterprise customer experienced approximately a fourfold performance improvement after adopting ARC and related products.

International Expansion Continues

International growth remains a strategic priority, with Paycom expanding in Europe and recently adding a large enterprise customer in Mexico. Management said the Mexican customer relationship has been progressing very well, supporting the company’s broader global ambitions.

Security and Data Control Matter to Clients

Management said security is a top concern for customers, particularly the ability to know exactly where their data resides. Paycom’s controlled infrastructure and data-center model were presented as important advantages for client confidence and data governance.

Fourth-Quarter Comparison Will Be Tougher

Paycom cautioned that the fourth quarter faces a difficult comparison with the prior year, when results benefited from a particularly strong period. Calendar anomalies and normal quarterly fluctuations could also affect the year-over-year presentation, even as underlying operations remain healthy.

In-App Purchasing Is Still Early

Self-service purchases of additional products through the Paycom app are becoming more meaningful and continue to grow. However, management said this channel remains small compared with the opportunities identified and handled by client relationship representatives.

International Data-Center Plans Remain Under Review

Paycom continues to evaluate possible data-center investments tied to international expansion and data-sovereignty requirements. Management said it is willing to invest further when doing so makes sense for clients, but did not provide a specific spending figure.

2026 Guidance Moves Higher

Paycom expects 2026 revenue of $2.213 billion to $2.218 billion, representing about 8% growth, while recurring and other revenue is expected to rise nearly 9%. Adjusted EBITDA is projected at $1.069 billion to $1.079 billion, with a midpoint margin of 48.5%, 550 basis points above the 2025 margin.

Cash Flow and Cost Outlook

Management expects approximately $107 million of interest on client funds, stock-based compensation near 3% of revenue, capital expenditures around 6%, and GAAP and non-GAAP tax rates of 29% and 27%, respectively. Paycom continues to expect very strong full-year free cash flow and stronger cash generation in 2027, while sales and marketing will remain a major focus next year.

Paycom’s call showed a business gaining operating leverage while expanding its automation platform and client value proposition. Strong cash flow, disciplined capital allocation, rising adoption of AI tools, and higher guidance outweighed concerns about the fourth-quarter comparison and the still-small in-app purchasing channel.

Overall, Paycom’s earnings call pointed to solid financial momentum and improving efficiency. Investors will be watching whether the company can sustain its margin gains, broaden automation adoption, and convert its growing product pipeline and international opportunity into continued growth.
